issues.description: Captures any issues that occurred while deserializing from filesystem

cleanupInterval.description: How often we scan the sessions for expiration.

idleTimeout.description:
How long a session must be idle before being closed. This means being removed from memory, and if #autoRestore is
true, being saved to the database.

restoreTimeout.description:
How long a session must be unused before its persisted state is discarded. After this period, auto-restore is no
longer possible.

doNotAutoRestore.description: Disallow sessions to be saved to the database and auto-restored when next accessed.

title:
Options for the ImplLanguage.Session types.

These revolve around the fact that session state is maintained in the server address space, and we need to clean up
to avoid core leaks. There is a stateless connection between the client and server so we use an idle period to
determine when the session can be removed from memory.

By default, session state is saved in the database when a session is dropped from memory and we will attempt to
recreate the session when accessed later ("auto-restore").

Note that there is a single configuration shared across all sub-types of ImplLanguage.Session.
name: ImplLanguage.Session.Config
